cast.name: Mr. Arthur Gerrard

surface_summary: A burned body is found in a rick, initially identified as Reginald Reed, a broker with an insurance policy. The investigation reveals inconsistencies in the identification, suggesting the body is not Reed's but that of his partner, Arthur Gerrard, who is suspected of faking his death. The case appears to be a complex insurance fraud involving murder and disguise.
accepted_facts: The burned body was found with distinctive objects bearing initials 'R.R.'
A dental plate found near the scene fits the burned body but not Reed
Arthur Gerrard appeared in court but later committed suicide when confronted
Reginald Reed and Arthur Gerrard were business partners with financial troubles
inferred_conclusions: The burned body is Reginald Reed's
Arthur Gerrard is innocent and a victim of mistaken identity
The death was accidental or suicide without foul play
mechanism_description: Reginald Reed and Arthur Gerrard conspired to fake Reed's death to claim insurance money. Reed was murdered, and his body was disguised with Gerrard's belongings to mislead identification. Gerrard assumed Reed's identity temporarily but committed suicide when exposed. The dental plate mismatch and distinctive objects revealed the deception.
delivery_path: Reed and Gerrard planned to abscond and realize assets
Reed was murdered and his body placed in the rick
Distinctive objects with Reed's initials were placed with the body
Gerrard disguised himself as Reed to claim insurance
Gerrard appeared in court under assumed identity
Gerrard was exposed by dental plate evidence
outcome_result: The true identity of the burned body is revealed as Gerrard, who murdered Reed and faked his death, leading to Gerrard's suicide and the resolution of the insurance fraud.

false_assumption.statement: The burned body found in the rick is that of Reginald Reed.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The body was found with Reed's personal effects including pipes with his initials and a distinctive watch-chain, and the dental plate was thought to fit the skull. These strong identifiers led everyone to accept the body's identity.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals that the body is actually that of Walter Jarman (alias Arthur Gerrard), and that the personal effects were deliberately placed to mislead identification and cover up a murder and insurance fraud.

supporting_points: He was seen in court claiming to be alive after the death
He had a motive to gain insurance money
He was associated with the victim and had access
The caretaker recognized him as Reed
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The caretaker only saw his overcoat and not his face, and the dental plate evidence contradicted his identity

red_herrings.description: Thomas Fletcher, a pickpocket found dead with stolen watches, was initially suspected of the murder of James Harewood.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Fletcher was found with Harewood's stolen property and was near the crime scene.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Fletcher was a secondary thief who picked the pocket of the actual murderer and was killed separately.

red_herrings.description: Harold Bowker was suspected of robbing the Blowgrave family and setting fire to lure them out.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: He was found spying on the excavation and had possession of some stolen items.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Bowker returned most stolen items and was identified by fingerprints; the scarab was the key to the real mystery, not the robbery.

closed_circle.rationale: The investigation focused on the two business partners involved in the insurance policy and the death, with no other plausible suspects having access or motive.

discriminating_test.design: Compare the dental plate found near the burned body with the dental records and plaster casts of both Reginald Reed and Walter Jarman. The test involves fitting the plate to the plaster models of each man's jaws to verify the true identity of the body. This physical comparison is concrete and verifiable.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The dental plate fits Walter Jarman's jaws perfectly but not Reginald Reed's, proving the body is not Reed's but Jarman's.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The dental plate matches the plaster cast of Jarman's jaws and not Reed's, conclusively identifying the body.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the personal effects found with the body, the dental plate, and the testimony of witnesses including the caretaker and dental surgeon. The discrepancy in the dental plate and the identity of the body is highlighted, allowing attentive readers to question the initial identification. The presence of two men with differing footprints and the disguise of Gerrard are also presented, enabling the reader to deduce the true sequence of events.
